reasons: Only seven of the seventeen sections needing notes are visible here, so the rest of the file is not reviewed.
The layout numbers are hand-set with no visible source.
No tests are visible in the packet.

terms.meaning: A named pattern for one kind of facility, such as a solar farm.
An expected main part of a facility, with the position and shape it should take in a schematic.
Reducing a word to a shared root, so that turbine and turbines are treated as the same term.
Words that, if present, make an archetype unlikely.
A word that adds a set score to an archetype when found, with stronger words having higher numbers.
Combined-cycle gas turbine plant: a gas turbine whose exhaust heats steam for a second turbine.
Heat recovery steam generator: the boiler that uses turbine exhaust heat to make steam.
A one-sentence rule describing the arrangement an archetype must follow.
A Python shorthand for a simple record type. A frozen one cannot be changed after it is created.

used_by: Other modules that call get_archetype or classify_facility are not visible in this packet.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Registry header and imports
sections.what: Sets the registry version to 1.0.0 and brings in the stemming helper, the confidence and hypothesis types, and the record helpers.
sections.why: Likely reason: the version number lets saved classifications be traced to the rules that produced them.
sections.watch_out: Changing the rules without changing the version makes past results hard to compare.

sections.name: CanonicalRole
sections.title: Canonical role record
sections.what: Describes one expected part of a facility: its identifier, the stemmed evidence words that point to it, its position in the schematic, its shape hint and the reason for its place.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app say why a part is drawn where it is.
sections.watch_out: The position is a schematic value, not a surveyed one.

sections.name: Archetype
sections.title: Facility archetype record
sections.what: Describes one facility type: its identifier, label, weighted keywords, negative keywords, its roles and its invariant sentence.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps every rule for one facility type together in one place.
sections.watch_out: Negative keywords can rule out a correct match if they are chosen too broadly.

sections.name: _role (part 1)
sections.title: Role helper and nuclear archetype start
sections.what: Builds a canonical role from a short keyword string by turning each word into its stem. Then starts the list of archetypes with the nuclear power station: its weighted keywords, its negative keywords, and its first roles for containment, fuel handling, turbine hall, switchyard and cooling.
sections.why: Likely reason: writing each role with a keyword string keeps the long list short and readable.
sections.watch_out: The position numbers are hand-set. Reason for the specific values is not stated in the code.

sections.name: _role (part 2)
sections.title: Nuclear layout tail and gas plant archetype
sections.what: Finishes the nuclear archetype with its layout sentence about containment, turbine island and grid connection. Then defines the combined-cycle gas plant: weighted keywords for gas, turbine, heat recovery boiler, stack, steam and condenser, negative keywords for reactor, containment and tracker, and roles for the gas turbine, heat recovery boiler, stack, steam hall and switchyard.
sections.why: Likely reason: the gas plant's layout follows the order of the gas train, with the steam hall beside it.
sections.watch_out: The steam hall and switchyard positions are hand-set, so they must not be read as measured distances.

sections.name: _role (part 3)
sections.title: Solar and transmission archetype start
sections.what: Defines the solar farm archetype: weighted keywords for solar, module, tracker, string, inverter and photovoltaic, negative keywords for turbine, reactor and underground, and roles for the module array, inverter skid and grid tie. Starts the transmission archetype with its keywords and its first role for the route.
sections.why: Likely reason: solar and transmission are visually very different, so their keywords and negative terms separate them from other types.
sections.watch_out: Tracker is a keyword for both solar and gas plants in this file, so it is not distinctive on its own.

sections.name: _role (part 4)
sections.title: Transmission roles and underground mine start
sections.what: Finishes the transmission archetype with its substation role and its layout sentence about towers and conductors. Then starts the underground mine archetype: weighted keywords for underground, tunnel, shaft, decline, drawpoint and similar terms, negative keywords for reactor and solar, and roles for the mine network, crusher, conveyor, stockpile and process block.
sections.why: Likely reason: mines and transmission lines have very different layouts, so each gets its own role list.
sections.watch_out: The underground mine archetype is cut off in this packet, so its invariant and remaining roles are not reviewed here.

sections.name: _role (part 5)
sections.title: Mining template ending and open-pit template
sections.what: Finishes one mining template and defines the open-pit mine template. The template lists words that suggest an open pit, such as pit, bench, haul and crusher, and the parts that a pit facility would include.
sections.why: Likely reason: each facility type needs its own layout template so the 3D view can place parts in a plausible arrangement.
sections.watch_out: The word weights are hand-set, so adding or changing a word here changes which facility type wins for every project that uses it.

sections.name: _role (part 6)
sections.title: Process plant template
sections.what: Defines the refinery or process plant template, with its own words (vessel, flare, tank, pipe rack) and the parts placed in it, such as mill, thickener, cyclone, pipe rack, tank farm and flare.
sections.why: Likely reason: process plants are laid out as flows of linked units, so they need a separate template from mines or buildings.
sections.watch_out: Some words, such as process and tank, also appear in other templates, so they can push a project toward the wrong facility type.

sections.name: _role (part 7)
sections.title: Process plant layout and building template
sections.what: Ends the process plant template and defines the building template, a single-part layout for floor plates around a core. Its words cover floors, storeys, cores, facades and hospitals.
sections.why: Likely reason: buildings are described by stacked floors around a service core, which needs its own simple template.
sections.watch_out: The building template has only one part, so it cannot show separate service zones; the description text is also used as the reason shown to the user.

sections.name: _role (part 8)
sections.title: Wind farm template
sections.what: Defines the wind farm template, with words such as wind, turbine, nacelle, blade and monopile, and parts for turbines and a substation that connects them through collector cables.
sections.why: Likely reason: wind farms are a turbine field tied to one grid connection point, which needs a template built around that shape.
sections.watch_out: The substation part is placed at a fixed offset, so changing the layout spacing changes where the grid tie appears.

sections.name: _role (part 9)
sections.title: Water treatment template and data centre start
sections.what: Defines the water or wastewater treatment template, with its stages from inlet to outlet, and begins the data centre template with its words and its data hall part.
sections.why: Likely reason: treatment plants move water through stages in sequence, so the template follows that flow.
sections.watch_out: The treatment template and the data centre template reuse common words such as tank, filter and basin, which can cause close scores between them.

sections.name: _role (part 10)
sections.title: Data centre and linear infrastructure templates
sections.what: Completes the data centre template with its power and cooling parts, then defines the road, rail and bridge template, with a route part and bridge parts placed along it.
sections.why: Likely reason: data centres repeat identical halls beside power and cooling blocks, while linear works follow a route measured by distance.
sections.watch_out: Linear templates depend on distance words such as chainage, so projects that do not use those words will not match this template well.

sections.name: get_archetype
sections.title: Unknown template fallback
sections.what: Places an empty placeholder template behind the unknown facility label. A lookup by identifier returns it when no template matches the given identifier.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app needs a safe answer for facility types it does not recognise, rather than an error.
sections.watch_out: A mistyped identifier silently returns the unknown placeholder instead of failing, so a typo can look like a missing facility type.

sections.name: _matches
sections.title: Word matching for templates
sections.what: Decides whether a word from a schedule matches a template word. A match is an exact word or a shared start of at least four letters on both sides.
sections.why: Likely reason: schedule text uses many forms of the same word, such as plural or related forms, so loose matching catches them.
sections.watch_out: Short template words are matched exactly, so changing the four-letter minimum changes many scores at once.

sections.name: classify_facility (part 1)
sections.title: Scoring each facility template
sections.what: Scores every template against the schedule words, adding weights for each matching word and subtracting penalties for negative words, then sorts the templates. If the best score is under 8, the result is the unknown facility type with a low confidence.
sections.why: Likely reason: the score threshold stops a few stray words from creating a confident facility label.
sections.watch_out: The threshold of 8 is a fixed number, so small changes to any weight or threshold can change the result for many projects.

sections.name: classify_facility (part 2)
sections.title: Confidence and final facility result
sections.what: Measures how far the best template beats the second best and how many matching words the schedule has. It then sets a high, medium or low confidence and returns the best facility type, the close alternate, the top evidence words and the limits of the answer.
sections.why: Likely reason: a small gap between the best and second-best template means the answer is uncertain, so the low confidence case is sent to a review list.
sections.watch_out: The limitations text always says the result comes from schedule words, not geometry or surveys, so that message must stay in any screen that shows the result.

summary: A versioned registry of facility types such as nuclear plants, gas combined-cycle plants, solar farms, transmission lines and underground mines. Each type lists weighted keywords that suggest it, keywords that rule it out, and the expected layout of its main parts. Only the first part of the file is visible in this packet.
purpose: Gives the app a fixed, reviewable list of what each facility type looks like, so it can guess a facility type from its documents and show a plausible arrangement.
why: Likely reason: keeping the rules in data, with a version number, makes them easy to review and to change deliberately. Reason for the specific numbers is not stated in the code.
how: A helper builds each canonical role from a short keyword string. Each archetype then lists its weighted keywords, its negative keywords, its roles with positions and shape hints, and a one-sentence invariant that describes the expected arrangement. The collection of archetypes is held in one fixed tuple. Other code, including the functions named get_archetype and classify_facility, reads this tuple. Those functions are not visible in this packet.
inputs: Keywords and layout values are hand-written here. Matching against a document is done by other code using the classifier module.
outputs: A fixed tuple of archetype records and the registry version string, used by the classification functions.
risks: The layout positions are hand-set numbers. They are not measured from any source, so the drawing must not be read as surveyed. A wrong keyword weight or a negative keyword that is too broad can make a facility fail to match. The file continues past the lines visible here.
debug: If a facility is classified wrongly, check the weights and negative keywords for the candidate types first. Check the registry version when comparing results over time. Check the stemmed keyword matching in the classifier if a word that should match does not.
